newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai grains/oilseeds active, mills buy corn.
newsitem.headline: Thai grains/oilseeds active, mills buy corn.

text.p: Thai poultry exporters bought up to 38,000 tonnes of corn from Argentina despite lingering confusion over the government's policy on zero-tariff imports this year, trade sources said on Tuesday.
The purchase was done recently. The vessel Rodosi was expected to leave a port in Brazil where it was loading up to 15,000 tonnes of soymeal soon and be here by May, they said.
The deal was likely to be done at around US$150 per tonne on a c&f basis, they added.

The slight fall in prices of Chicago soybeans and soymeal also attracted buying interest. But buying orders were so far moderate over the week since many in the industry expected prices to drop further.
Traders said feedmillers and exporters bought around 15,000-20,000 tonnes of soymeal from various origins last week.
"We expect to secure more orders as prices dip," said one trader in Bangkok.
Market sources confirmed that Thanakorn Vegetable Oil, one of the major oil crushers, had bought 50,000 tonnes of soybeans from Brazil. The shipment was expected to arrive in May.
Another major crusher, Thai Vegetable Oil, was still seeking 50,000 tonnes of soybeans for June shipment. Traders expected the deal to be concluded soon.
The prices of local soymeal edged up to 10.30 baht a kg while locally-crushed imported beans also firmed to 9.90 baht a kg. The corn price also rose to 4.60-4.65 baht a kg.
